Performers
Orchestre de la Suisse Romande (orchestra), Ernest Ansermet (conductor) Documented

The instrumental movement has no choral part. No orchestral soloist or complete roster is identified or inferred. The unresolved Sirènes chorus does not enter this movement.

[1] [3] [4] [5]
Work version
Original orchestral work; exact performing edition unestablished Unknown

The sources identify the work and movement, but not the parts or revision used in October 1951. The original Fromont/Kalmus and 1930 Jobert full scores were viewed. Musical annotations use shared principal passages; no claim that Ansermet follows every detail of the revised edition, no cut/repeat-order certification, and no bar-accurate score alignment. Orchestra states are explicitly provisional passage estimates, not audio instrument detection.

[1] [7] [8]
Recorded
October 1951 Documented

Month and year are corroborated. Stuart’s [a] Nocturnes has no exact day: the 10th and 12th in the shared session heading refer to other works. The 1951 session must not be described as a 1951 publication.

[1] [3] [5]
Place
Victoria Hall, Geneva, Switzerland Documented

Venue is independently supplied by the session discography and the matching London CD catalogue record.

[3] [5]
Label
Decca Documented

Original British LP label; London LL 530 is the separately dated June 1952 issue in Stuart.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
LXT 2637 Documented

First British issue March 1952. Side A contains the three Nocturnes; side B Ravel’s Rapsodie espagnole. Original label images were not present in the IA item, so the date relies on the discography rather than an inspected LP label.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Side A; suite master series SAR587–SAR592 Documented

IA identifies the side and track order; Stuart assigns SAR587–⁠92 to Nocturnes as a whole. No individual movement matrix, LP runout, take number or pressing identification is established, and none is extrapolated from the six-number series.

[1] [3]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No digital-transfer engineer is credited. IA account identity is not a transfer credit. Victor Olof (producer) and Gil Went (engineer) are documented for the original Decca session, not for this digital transfer.

[2] [3]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded/published on IA on 26 December 2021. That is not evidence for when the physical record was transferred.

[2]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Original FLAC and derived VBR MP3 are listed, but playback equipment, equalisation, de-clicking, noise reduction, pitch correction and intervening edits are undocumented. No listening or processing-quality claim is made.

[2]
Composition rights
Public-domain underlying composition under ordinary life-plus-70 terms Inferred, not documented

Debussy died in 1918; the original score was published in 1900–⁠01. Original and 1930 score pages were consulted as historical score evidence. This assessment of the composition is separate from sound-recording rights and does not claim rights in a modern edition, scan or arrangement.

[10] [6] [11] [7] [8]
Recording rights
Rule 3 territorial basis: EU sound recording first published before 1963; US public-domain status not established Documented

LXT 2637 was issued in March 1952, not 1951. Under the ordinary former EU 50-year publication term this predates expiry before the 1 November 2013 extension threshold. This is the project’s territorial pre-1963 basis, not a Creative Commons licence or a worldwide public-domain claim. US status has not been established. IA supplies no open-licence URL; the upload alone does not grant rights.

Claude Debussy, II. Fêtes — Animé et très rythmé from Nocturnes; Orchestre de la Suisse Romande, Ernest Ansermet. Recorded October 1951, Victoria Hall, Geneva; Decca LXT 2637, first issued March 1952. Internet Archive transfer, transfer engineer unknown. Territorial Rule 3 basis only; US public-domain status not established.

  2. Internet Archive original-file and derivative metadata — metadata and files arrays; original FLAC files and VBR MP3 derivatives. No licence URL or named digital-transfer engineer is supplied. Item publication/upload date 26 December 2021 does not date the recording or LP.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Philip Stuart, Decca discography, S section, session S080 — PDF p. 24, S080: October 1951, Victoria Hall, Geneva; Victor Olof, producer; Gil Went, engineer; [a] Nocturnes, SAR587–⁠92; [ab] LXT 2637 March 1952, LL 530 June 1952. Day marks 10 and 12 apply to [c] and [d], not [a]. CD [a] POCL 4628 = 466217.2.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Decca Eloquence: Debussy Orchestral Works, 4800127 — Official label reissue identifies the 1951 Nocturnes and OSR/Ernest Ansermet, describing its first international CD release. Does not name the women’s chorus.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. CiNii Books BA44017886: La mer / Nocturnes / Jeux, London POCL-4628 — Notes give Nocturnes recorded October 1951, Victoria Hall, Geneva, with “Female Chorus”, Orchestre de la Suisse Romande and Ernest Ansermet. POCL-4628 / 466 217-2 matches Stuart S080’s 1951 reissue. No full chorus name is supplied.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. IMSLP work catalogue: Nocturnes, CD 98 (L.91) — Work information: composed 1897–⁠99; Fromont first publication 1900–⁠01; Nuages/Fêtes premiered 9 December 1900, complete work 27 October 1901, Paris, Camille Chevillard. Full-score edition and instrumentation listings.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Debussy, Nocturnes: original orchestral score, Kalmus reprint of Fromont — Indiana University, Variations score BFJ7336. Viewable printed pages: Nuages 2, 13, 16, 18; Fêtes 19, 43, 48, 53, 69, 70. This is score evidence, not documentation of the edition on Ansermet’s desks.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Debussy, Nocturnes, édition définitive, Jobert 1930, plates J.J. 419–⁠421 — Sibley Music Library digitization; title and selected orchestral pages viewed: Nuages pp. 1–⁠2, 8, 11–⁠13, 15–⁠17; Fêtes pp. 18–⁠20, 33, 37–⁠39, 41–⁠42, 46–⁠48, 51–⁠52, 54, 58, 62, 66, 68–⁠69. Changes between the original and revised opening of Fêtes are not assigned to this performance.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Los Angeles Philharmonic programme note: Nocturnes — Debussy’s programme on decorative colour, Nuages and the Fêtes procession; first performances. Used for the stated programme, not the article’s discussion of gamelan chronology.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. Stephen Walsh, Claude Debussy, Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center — Dates 1862–⁠1918 and Middle Period section: Prélude 1891–⁠94, Nocturnes 1897–⁠99, Pelléas begun 1893; title’s connection with Whistler rather than Chopin.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  11. Directive 2006/116/EC on terms of copyright and related rights — Article 1(1), life plus 70 years; Article 3, former 50-year phonogram/performer terms; Article 8, calendar-year calculation. Territorial term framework, not a licence.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  12. Directive 2011/77/EU extending certain related-rights terms — Article 1 amendments to Articles 3 and 10 of Directive 2006/116/EC: the extended term applies to qualifying fixations still protected on 1 November 2013. Does not establish US public-domain status.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
